newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel approves 1996 investment budget increase.
newsitem.headline: Israel approves 1996 investment budget increase.

text.p: The Israeli parliament's finance committee approved a 300 million shekel increase in the 1996 Investment Centre budget, the Ministry of Industry and Trade said on Monday.
The centre, a ministry arm that approves capital investment subsidies, had requested the extra funding because it had already exhausted its budget and could not approve additional projects this year.
The centre's 1996 budget was originally 1.8 billion shekels.
David Baruch, the centre's director, told Reuters there were projects worth more than 800 million shekels awaiting approval.
"The extra budget will allow us to approve part of the requests," he said.
The government plans to cut investment subsidies in 1997. Under the proposal, which still needs parliamentary approval, grants in top priority areas would be cut from 34 percent to 20 percent.

Projects that are not approved this year will get the lower subsidies next year. Vishay Intertechnology has said that if its proposed $50 million plant in the town of Ofakim is not approved this year, it may reconsider its investment.
"We will not be able to approve all the projects proposed and we still have to decide which are priority projects," Baruch said. "I cannot comment on any particular project at the moment."
